title: Draft and Preview Mode
summary: Let editors preview unpublished content through a protected preview path.
nestedConcepts: Show draft content in preview mode
Keep drafts out of public caches

subtopics.title: Show draft content in preview mode
subtopics.explanation: Next.js Draft Mode uses a cookie to let an authorized preview request render unpublished content. The page must fetch the draft version from the content source and avoid serving it as a public cached page. Keep the ordinary published route fast and cacheable.

subtopics.title: Protect the preview entry point
subtopics.explanation: The route that enables preview must verify a secret or authenticated editor session before setting the draft cookie. Do not expose the secret in client-side code or logs. Reject missing and invalid credentials before making any draft content available.

subtopics.title: Keep drafts out of public caches
subtopics.explanation: Draft pages may contain unpublished information, so they must not be stored in a shared public cache. Configure caching based on the preview cookie and content source. Test a draft request and a normal request separately to ensure one user cannot receive another user’s preview.

subtopics.title: Limit preview access duration
subtopics.explanation: Preview access should last only as long as an editor needs it. Provide a way to leave Draft Mode and clear the cookie, and use the platform’s secure cookie settings. A short-lived, explicit preview flow reduces accidental exposure from a shared browser.

subtopics.title: Test preview and published paths
subtopics.explanation: Verify that an authorized preview shows draft content, an unauthorized request is rejected, and exiting preview returns to published content. Also check response headers and caching behavior. A test that only checks the page text can miss a private response being cached publicly.

foundations.overview: Draft mode allows a Next.js site to show unpublished content, often from a content system. Preview access must be protected and scoped. Disable shared caching for private drafts and ensure preview tokens cannot leak through URLs or logs.
foundations.mentalModel: A proof copy lets the editor review a page before it goes on the public shelf.
foundations.whyItMatters: Editors can review changes before publication without exposing them to all visitors.

keyTakeaways: Preview mode changes how content is fetched or cached.
Protect entry routes with a secret or authenticated workflow.
Test exit behavior and published content separately.
